blocks.text: There were Libertarian candidates across the state running for office for the 2023 elections. Of the 18 candidates, there were 6 victories.
In Chautauqua County, Ryan Sanders was re-elected Sherman Village Trustee, running for one of two positions in a race with only two candidates.

blocks.text: In Steuben County, Angela Einwachter was re-elected to Prattsburgh Town Council in a two-way race with two seats available.

blocks.text: In Oneida County, there were two victories. Oneida County Libertarian Party Chair Keith Redhead was elected Ava Town Supervisor in a contested two-way race against Republican candidate David C. Mathis, Sr. Also in the Town of Ava, Kathleen Redhead was elected Tax Collector—the first victory for the Libertarian Party of New York for that type of office.

blocks.text: We now proceed to the 2024 election cycle!

The second Empire State Freedom Summit was held at the Rail Line in Syracuse on November 10-11, 2023. The event began on Friday evening with entertainment from comedian, writer, and author Lou Perez. Following this, 2024 Libertarian Presidential candidates were given an opportunity to address the attendees and take questions. Two such candidates were present for this opportunity: Joshua Smith and Mike ter Maat.

blocks.text: On Saturday, the event began in the afternoon with three speakers who had never spoken at an LPNY event before: Shane Hazel, a Libertarian candidate who spoke on Bitcoin; Dr. Clayton Baker of the Brownstone Institute, who spoke on medical freedom; and Dan Warmus, founder of Auditing Erie County, who spoke on First Amendment Audits. Saturday evening concluded the event with a fundraiser, including a silent auction.
